Title: Two Malaysians injured by Typhoon Champi in stable condition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two Malaysians who sustained minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi in Taiwan are receiving
treatment at separate hospitals
and their conditions are reported to be stable.
Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC) President Bong Yik Jui said the victims, both 57, were receiving treatment at Dali Jen Ai Hospital in Taichung and Miaoli Daqian Hospital in Miaoli, respectively.
"We contacted them separately and confirmed that they are in stable condition," he told Bernama.
He added that one of the Malaysians had been discharged from hospital after receiving treatment.
Bong said the MFTC would closely monitor developments related to Typhoon Champi, particularly its implications for the safety and welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan.
"MFTC will remain in contact with the Malaysian community through existing communication channels," he said.
Media reported that Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, leaving one
dead and more than 500 injured.
The typhoon also damaged hundreds of buildings, disrupted electricity supply, and forced flight cancellations.
As of August, this year, there were 34,833 Malaysians in Taiwan, including 7,615 students.
Bong urged Malaysians residing in or visiting Taiwan to monitor local weather advisories and adhere to safety instrutions and evacuation orders issued by local authorities.
Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information concerning other Malaysian nationals who may require assistance in the affected areas, are urged to contact MFTC in Taipei at +886 972 349 343 or via email at mwtaipei@kln.gov.my.
Bong also urged Malaysians in Taiwan to register and regularly update their contact details through the e-Konsular portal at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my (https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my/) to facilitate timely communication and consular assistance, particularly during emergencies.
He also encouraged Malaysians to follow the MFTC's social media channels for the latest updates and advisories.
The MFTC serves as Malaysia's official representative office in Taipei, performing consular functions similar to those of Malaysian diplomatic and consular missions abroad and providing assistance and support to Malaysians in Taiwan. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan education dept probing claims students served alcohol at dinner
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Education Department is finalising an investigation regarding allegations of students from a school being involved in the serving of alcoholic beverages during a dinner event held by the school's alumni association on Sept 5.
In a statement today, the department said that school students should not be involved in activities involving the handling or serving of alcoholic beverages.
Based on initial information, the event was organised by the alumni association outside the school premises, while the school and the association denied allegations of student involvement in the serving of
alcoholic beverages
, it said.
The department said that the investigation into complaints received through the Public Complaint Management System (SISPAA) also includes an examination of the school's compliance with procedures.
"If there are any violations of regulations or negligence in the performance of duties, appropriate action will be taken based on the applicable regulations," read the statement.
The department emphasised that the welfare, safety, and dignity of students are always a priority and that it (the department) will ensure that the investigation results are thoroughly reviewed before any follow-up actions are taken.

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning in 9 states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 6pm today.
The warning covers Perlis, Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak), as well as Langkawi and Kubang Pasu in Kedah.
The warning also applies to Kota Tinggi and Johor Baru in Johor; Cameron Highlands in Pahang; Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus and Setiu in Terengganu; and Jeli, Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas and Tumpat in Kelantan.
In Sabah, the affected areas are Kudat; Sandakan; Tawau (Tawau, Kunak and Semporna); the West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang and Tuaran); and the Interior (Tambunan, Sook, Keningau, Beaufort, Tenom, Sipitang and Pensiangan).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Bintulu (Tatau and Sebauh); Kapit (Kapit and Belaga); Limbang; Miri (Marudi, Bario, Beluru and Telang Usan); and Sibu (Selangau). — BERNAMA

Title: PM: Govt prepared to absorb fuel subsidy cost of up to RM45b a year
Article:
Bernama
MELAKA: The government is prepared to absorb an increase in fuel subsidy costs, which could reach RM45 billion annually amid a surge in global crude oil prices, rather than pass the burden on to the people through higher fuel prices.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government remained committed to maintaining the price of RON95 petrol at RM1.99 per litre despite international crude oil prices climbing to between US$120 and US$130 a barrel.
He said the move was aimed at shielding the public, particularly low- and middle-income groups, from the impact of rising global fuel prices and the resulting pressure on household expenses.
"If oil prices continue to surge, the cost borne by the government could reach between RM42 billion and RM45 billion a year. If we raise fuel prices in line with market rates, people would have to pay an additional RM2 or RM3, or at least RM5 a day.
"Imagine those who have to send their children to school and go to work themselves. That could mean an extra RM10 a day. It is better for the government to bear the burden than to burden the people, our parents," he said at the 'Sentuhan Kasih Madani' Programme and the launch of the National Cost of Living Action Plan 2030 at the Hang Jebat Sports Complex in Krubong.
Anwar said global crude oil prices had nearly doubled from around US$70 a barrel previously, putting many countries under mounting cost-of-living pressures.
However, he said the government had chosen to continue absorbing a substantial portion of fuel subsidy costs to prevent consumers from facing steep petrol price increases if prices were allowed to float in line with market rates.
He also rejected the view that generous subsidies made the people overly dependent on government assistance, stressing that policies must take into account the realities faced by low-income households.
Anwar said the government would continue to balance efforts to drive economic growth with its responsibility to ensure that national progress translated into a better standard of living and greater well-being for the people.
He said the country's economic success should not be measured solely by growth, investment and trade, but also by the tangible benefits it delivered in improving the people's standard of living and well-being.
He said efforts to drive economic growth, including through mastery of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductors, must go hand in hand with addressing the people's basic needs, particularly the cost of living, education, healthcare and employment opportunities.
"We are not talking merely about figures and statistics, but about people.
"The government's approach is guided by the principle of 'reaching for the sky while remaining rooted in the ground', which requires the country to continue exploring new fields of knowledge and technology without neglecting human values, ethics, culture and the well-being of the people at the grassroots level," he said.
Also present were Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali and his deputy, Datuk Fuziah Salleh. — BERNAMA

Title: Melaka polls: Damian Yeo would quit politics rather than give Bemban to Bersatu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Melaka DAP chairman Damian Yeo has vowed to quit politics rather than accept any move by Pakatan Harapan (PH) to cede the Bemban state seat to Bersatu in the upcoming Melaka election.
The former Duyong assemblyman said he learnt of the possibility while discussing candidates, campaign strategies and the political landscape with another former Melaka DAP chairman.
"But when I heard that the plan under PH Plus could involve giving up Bemban to Bersatu, my immediate reaction was... Forget it, I am out," he said in a Facebook post.
Yeo said the wounds of past political betrayals remained fresh, making it difficult for him to accept any proposed cooperation with Bersatu.
"The wound from being stabbed in the back is still fresh. Some political betrayals are simply too difficult to forget, let alone forgive.
"I have been there, done that, and paid the price," he said.
He said he had decided to withdraw from political activities, including campaigning in the Melaka election.
His remarks come amid speculation over a possible electoral arrangement between PH and Bersatu.
On Sept 19, Melaka PH chairman
Datuk Seri Adly Zahari confirmed
that discussions were being held with Bersatu on a possible PH Plus collaboration.
However, Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said on Wednesday that PH would contest the state election on its own, without cooperating with other parties, including Bersatu.
He also said DAP intended to contest eight seats, including Bemban, which its former chairman Datuk Tey Kok Kiew lost in the 2021 state election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Worker killed, another injured in suspected drink-driving crash in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 28-year-old worker was killed when a drunk driver rammed his car into him while he was installing warning signs along Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar early today.
City police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the 26-year-old driver recorded an alcohol breath screening reading of 64mg/100ml and was arrested and remanded for three days until Monday to assist in investigations.
He said the accident occurred at about 5am when the car, travelling from Jalan Damansara towards Jalan Parlimen, lost control and struck two workers in the left lane.
"The victim, a supervisor, was pronounced dead while receiving treatment, while another worker, a 49-year-old lorry driver, sustained injuries to his head and right hand. The lorry driver is receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital. The car driver escaped uninjured.
"The five workers, comprising a supervisor, a lorry driver and three Bangladeshi workers, had been carrying out warning sign installation works under a Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) contract.
"The work began at 11pm on Oct 23 and ended at 4am today," he said in a statement.
Zamzuri said the case was being investigated under Sections 44(1)(b) and 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Section 44 of the Act covers offences involving driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs that causes death.
Those with information about the incident are urged to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 251 sexual offence cases involving tertiary students reported in 8 months
Article:
MELAKA: A total of 251 sexual offence cases involving higher education students were reported between January and August this year.
Citing police statistics, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said the figures underscored the need for sustained efforts to improve sexual safety in educational institutions.
She said the Waja Siswa Squad, part of the Women Against Crime initiative, was established to promote volunteerism and community involvement in raising awareness and addressing violence against women.
"In tackling this issue, we must not only understand how to protect ourselves but also how to help others appropriately," she said when officiating the Melaka-level Waja Siswa Squad programme at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) here today.
Also present were the ministry's deputy secretary-general (Management) Datuk Ruziah Shafei and Women's Development Department director-general Hanani Sapit.
Lim said violence against women and sexual harassment should not be taken lightly, as they could take various forms, including threats, humiliation, emotional manipulation, financial control and sexual abuse.
She said actions dismissed as jokes or expressions of affection should not be normalised if they violated personal boundaries, caused fear or made someone feel threatened.
She urged students to understand their rights and learn how to seek help if they experienced sexual harassment.
Lim also called on UTeM students, regardless of gender, to raise awareness among their peers and help create a campus environment that rejects violence and promotes healthy relationships.
She said the programme was expected to strengthen student participation in efforts to make campuses safer.
Lim said 340,667 volunteers had joined the Waja Squad nationwide as of September, comprising 264,461 women and 76,206 men.
She said men's participation as allies was important in promoting respect for women, rejecting harassment and encouraging healthy relationships, stressing that preventing violence was not solely women's responsibility.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Terengganu govt extends condolences over Tengku Baderul Zaman's passing
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu state government has extended its condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, and the entire royal family following the passing of Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah today.
The condolences were conveyed by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, who also expressed them on behalf of the people of Terengganu in a statement on his Facebook page.
"May Allah SWT forgive all the late Tengku Baderul Zaman's sins, shower His mercy upon him, accept his good deeds and place his soul among His faithful and righteous servants.
"May all members of the family and the royal household be granted fortitude and strength in facing this loss," he said.
Samsuri said the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, had decreed a three-day mourning period beginning today.
"The people of Terengganu are requested to respect the mourning period and comply with the stipulated rules, including the dress code when paying their last respects to the late Tengku Baderul Zaman," he said.
Tengku Baderul Zaman, the younger brother of Sultan Mizan,
died at 1.20am today at Gleneagles Hospital
in Kuala Lumpur.

Title: Sabah Pan Borneo 95pct complete, contractors given until year-end
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Contractors handling three critical work packages of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project along the Putatan, Penampang, Inanam, Sepanggar and Tuaran stretches have been instructed to complete the remaining construction works by the end of this year.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said completing the three packages was crucial to improving traffic flow around Kota Kinabalu and reducing congestion on existing routes.
He said Work Packages 6 (WP06), 7 (WP07) and 8 (WP08) were nearing completion but could not yet be fully opened as several sections were still under construction.
"I have personally asked for construction works along these stretches to be completed by the end of this year. They must be completed by year-end. Once the Pan Borneo Highway is completed, traffic flow can be improved.
"This means vehicles that do not need to stop in Kota Kinabalu, particularly those heading directly to Beaufort and Papar, can use this route.
"So far, I have been informed that construction is 95 per cent complete, with only a few sections remaining. We will monitor the progress and ensure it is completed by the end of this year," he said after launching the Madani Kita @ Sepanggar programme in Manggatal, near today.
Mustapha, who is also Sepanggar member of parliament, was responding to questions about measures to address delays in the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, particularly along the stretches passing through his constituency.
The three packages comprise WP06 from Putatan to Inanam, WP07 from Inanam to Sepanggar, and WP08 from Sepanggar to Berungis Roundabout.
They are key components of the Kota Kinabalu Outer Ring Road, which is designed to divert some traffic away from the city centre.
Mustapha acknowledged that all three packages had been delayed and were considered critical because they involved urban routes that frequently experience congestion.
"We hope this stretch of the Pan Borneo Highway will be completed by the end of the year so that congestion on existing routes can be eased," he said.
Commenting on traffic congestion in Sepanggar, particularly before motorists enter the Pan Borneo Highway stretch near Kampung Tebobon, Mustapha said the problem stemmed from the concentration of traffic on existing roads, which were also used by heavy vehicles.
He said this had caused several sections of the road to deteriorate frequently, especially during rainy weather. The damage continued to recur despite repair works because of the weak road structure and constant use.
"The road damage is repaired, but the problem now is that the repairs do not last because the road is used daily.
"We have asked the Public Works Department (PWD) and the contractors to ensure the road is safe for users," he said.
Phase 1 of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project comprises 35 work packages spanning 706km.
The Auditor-General's Report 2/2026 stated that
only four of the 35 packages, or 11.4 per cent,
had been fully completed as at March 31, while the remaining 31 were still under implementation.
However, the figures refer to the number of packages fully completed, rather than the overall physical progress of the project.
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister and state Works and Utilities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam had earlier said physical progress under Phase 1A had reached 89.54 per cent as at Sept 25, compared with the scheduled progress of 96.23 per cent.
In a separate development, Mustapha said the Madani Kita @ Sepanggar programme was organised by the Sabah Federal Youth and Sports Department, with young people making up about 80 per cent of its participants.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Sharafuddin wants no Selangor resident left behind amid state's progress
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Despite Selangor's status as one of Malaysia's most developed states, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah remains concerned about subjects, particularly the poor and underprivileged, who continue to struggle with daily life.
Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said the Sultan's role as Head of the Islamic Religion in Selangor extended beyond safeguarding the faith and strengthening religious institutions to protecting the Muslim community's welfare while maintaining harmony with non-Muslims.
Salehuddin, who has known the Sultan for nearly 18 years and is a member of the Selangor Royal Council, said the ruler took his responsibility to safeguard his subjects' welfare, uphold the sanctity of Islam and ensure justice seriously.
"His Highness is always deeply concerned about matters affecting the Muslim community. Should there be instances where Muslims are oppressed, left without economic support or struck by misfortune, His Highness is the first to instruct us, the religious institutions, to take action," he told Bernama in an interview held in conjunction with the recent Silver Jubilee celebration of the Sultan's reign.
Salehuddin said the Sultan paid particular attention to low-income Muslims and those living in poverty, insisting that they be identified so assistance could reach them effectively.
"In every discussion, His Highness consistently reminds us that the poor and destitute must not be sidelined. He emphasises the need to compile data so that this group continues to receive the attention it needs," he said.
Despite his pride in Selangor's development, Sultan Sharafuddin has cautioned against measuring the state's success solely in economic terms while some of its people remain poor.
Salehuddin said the Sultan was aware of urban poverty, including residents of dilapidated flats where large families were forced to live in cramped two-room homes.
The Sultan has questioned the value of celebrating the state's progress if sections of society remain marginalised.
In response, he has directed religious institutions, including the Selangor Zakat Board, to identify asnaf, or zakat-eligible recipients, and ensure assistance reaches those who need it most.
Salehuddin said the Sultan had also said that state policies and budget allocations must address the housing, education and daily needs of underprivileged communities.
On strengthening Islam, Salehuddin said the Sultan wanted Muslims' aqidah (faith) preserved in accordance with the Ahli Sunnah wal Jamaah tradition, while measures were taken to curb deviant teachings and ideologies such as liberalism and pluralism.
He said religious institutions, including mosques and surau, must be managed professionally, particularly in administration and finance, to maintain public confidence.
The Sultan also wanted comprehensive religious programmes to reach urban and rural communities, including the B40 and other underprivileged groups, so that the benefits of development and welfare were shared more equitably.
At the same time, efforts to strengthen Islam must go hand in hand with respect for other religions to preserve social harmony.
Salehuddin said the Sultan viewed unity among Muslims and positive relations among people of different ethnic backgrounds and faiths as essential to national development.
Community leaders, he said, should promote unity rather than deepen divisions.
"His Highness expects community leaders never to act as the masterminds behind societal fragmentation. Instead, they should encourage Muslims and people of other ethnic groups to live in harmony and unity," he said.
The younger generation is another priority for the Sultan, who has repeatedly reminded Mais and the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) not to overlook young people when planning religious programmes at state, district, mosque and surau levels.
Salehuddin said Sultan Sharafuddin wanted targeted initiatives to draw young people to mosques and surau through activities suited to their interests, including sports and recreation after the Subuh (dawn) prayer.
Mosque and surau committees had also been urged to engage younger congregants and diversify activities to make religious institutions more welcoming.
"We must not focus solely on the adult or older generations when planning initiatives to enliven our mosques," he said.
Salehuddin said the Sultan had called on mosque and surau committees to move beyond conventional approaches and tailor programmes to different segments of society.
Through such efforts, mosques and surau could serve not only as places of worship but also as centres for learning, strengthening community ties, distributing aid and bringing young people closer to religion.
Ultimately, the Sultan's vision for the Muslim community extends beyond economic growth and strong religious institutions to caring for the poor, preserving social harmony and ensuring no one is left behind.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar extends condolences to Terengganu Sultan over brother's passing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, on the passing of His Royal Highness's younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Allah SWT would shower His mercy upon Tengku Baderul Zaman's soul, grant him forgiveness and place him among the righteous.
"May the Sultan of Terengganu and the entire royal family be granted fortitude and strength in facing this deeply felt loss. Al-Fatihah," the post read.
Tengku Baderul Zaman
died at 1.20am today
at Gleneagles Hospital.

Title: King and Queen extend condolences to Sultan of Terengganu on brother's passing
Article:

Title: Melaka polls: Wawasan wants to contest under PN logo, says Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) wants to contest the Melaka election under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) logo.
Its president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said the party preferred to use the coalition's logo, but would discuss alternatives if necessary.
"If possible, we want to use the PN logo. If not, we will have to sit down again as a team and decide which logo is best for us," he told reporters.
Hamzah said
PN had initiated legal action
after receiving a notice from the Registrar of Societies (RoS) suspending and subsequently deregistering the coalition on Oct 20.
"When we received the letter from the RoS, we took it to court as quickly as possible.
"That shows we believe the PN logo represents all of us, and that it is our team," he said.
On Oct 22, the High Court
granted PN a stay
against the RoS action pending the full disposal of its judicial
review, without ruling on the legality of the deregistration.
The ruling allows PN to continue its political activities while the legal challenge is pending.
PN election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor welcomed the decision, saying it would
allow the coalition to continue operating
pending the judicial review.
Sanusi had earlier said PN was prepared to contest the Melaka polls under the Pas moon logo if it could not use its own.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'My children were lying on the road': Father's horror after Johor crash
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A father was left devastated after one of his four children died and the other three were injured when the car they were travelling in skidded off Jalan Johor Baru-Melaka near Bagan last night.
Noorwandi A Rahim, 41, struggled to hold back his tears as he watched his children's condition before one of them succumbed to his injuries.
Recounting the incident,
Noorwandi said he received a call
from his younger sibling at about 10pm informing him that the car carrying his children, younger sister and brother-in-law had been involved in an accident.
He said he and his wife, Norfarahin Mohammad, 38, had just arrived home after having dinner together at a shopping mall.
"My wife and I were riding a motorcycle, while our children were in a car driven by my brother-in-law.
"When I arrived at the scene, I saw my children scattered on the road. Putera Muhaimin Qudrat, 16, was lying face down, with his face covered in sand and petrol.
"My wife and I immediately rushed to our other children, Puteri Nur Fairuza Balqis, 15, Putera Khairunas, 11, and Putera Aidin Firdaus, three. My brother-in-law, Nor Azlan Shaharudin, 27, was trapped in the driver's seat.
"I then laid Putera Muhaimin Qudrat down. He responded only once before falling silent.
"The medical team tried to revive him, but my son was pronounced dead," he said when met at the Forensic Department of Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail (HSNI).
Noorwandi said his youngest child, Putera Aidin Firdaus, was still receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) at the same hospital.
"Puteri Nur Fairuza Balqis suffered a fractured thigh, chest injuries and slight bleeding in the head, while Putera Khairunas sustained minor injuries and is now in stable condition.
"Putera Aidin Firdaus suffered bleeding in the head, as well as fractures to both arms, legs and a shoulder. He is currently under close observation by the medical team in the ICU.
"My younger sister, Rahmah A Rahim, 26, who is Nor Azlan's wife, is stable and has been warded. She told me that their car was hit from behind before the accident.
"The car then hit a bridge and another vehicle at a workshop before crashing into a coconut tree," he said.
Meanwhile, Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said preliminary investigations found that the car was travelling from Batu Pahat towards Parit Moin, Bagan, when the accident occurred.
He said the driver was believed to have lost control of the vehicle, causing it to skid and crash into a roadside tree.
"All injured victims are still receiving treatment at HSNI. The case is being investigated under the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless driving causing death," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shuhaily's position left to Home Ministry, Chief Secretary - Saifuddin
Article:
KULAI: The Home Ministry has left matters concerning the position of Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain to the ministry's secretary-general and the Chief Secretary to the Government.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the matter was being handled in accordance with existing civil service regulations.
"The matter is being handled between my ministry's secretary-general and the Chief Secretary to the Government," he said when asked to comment on the issue.
Saifuddin was speaking to reporters after launching the 78th National Registration Day celebration and the launch of the National Registration Department's (NRD) Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani (SAM) initiatives for 2026 at Kampung Melayu Sedenak today.
Commenting on criticism from opposition members of parliament, who claimed he had failed to mediate in the dispute involving MCBA and its personnel, Saifuddin said he accepted the criticism with an open mind.
However, he also questioned the ability of opposition leaders to play the role of peacemakers when their own parties were facing divisions, including a conflict between groups supporting Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
Earlier, opposition members of parliament questioned Saifuddin's failure, as Home Minister, to adopt a family-oriented approach in addressing the issue involving Shuhaily and the two police personnel.
During the debate on the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat, opposition members of parliament expressed hope that action against Shuhaily could be withdrawn.
They also questioned the speed of the prosecution process and whether there was a specific agenda, particularly in relation to the "corporate mafia" issue.
Shuhaily
pleaded not guilty
at the Sepang magistrate's court to two charges of voluntarily causing hurt to police personnel Faiz Saman and Ekmal Sofwan Dirman at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on Sept 28.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman returns from overseas holiday to find husband dead in massage chair
Article:
JASIN: A 54-year-old man was found dead in a massage chair at his home in Ayer Merbau, Bemban this morning.
Jasin police chief Superintendent Lee Robert said the man's body was found by his wife upon her return from a week-long holiday overseas.
"The wife contacted their child after finding her husband unconscious in the massage chair," he said when contacted.
"The case is currently classified as sudden death, and investigations are underway to determine the cause of death," he said.

Title: Asean needs a tribunal with teeth to tackle climate challenges
Article:
I have been breathing the haze, on and off, since I was a child. I was 14 in September 1997, when Sarawak declared a state of emergency after Kuching's air pollutant index (API) reading passed 500, and it later peaked near 800.
I was 30 in June 2013, when Muar's API hit 746. Now it is October 2026, and my son, who has asthma, is stuck indoors. Every trip outside is a risk.
On Oct 9, schools across Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Selangor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan and Johor were shut. Nothing in that timeline is new. What has run out is our patience.
For me, the "Asean Way" on dealing with regional issues has reached its limit, especially when it comes to haze. Asean signed its Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in 2002.
Indonesia, the last member to ratify it, deposited its instrument in January 2015, 13 years later. The agreement has no meaningful enforcement or dispute-resolution mechanism.
In a resource-constrained world, it means nobody is empowered to act when the sky turns brown. The Covid-19 pandemic showed the same gap, with each government improvising its solutions alone.
Thus, Asean needs a tribunal for environmental harm, built on the logic of the International Criminal Court (ICC), which prosecutes individuals for atrocity crimes.
Vanuatu, Fiji and Samoa proposed adding ecocide to the ICC's statute in September 2024. We should not wait for The Hague.
An Asean Environmental Tribunal would need four powers. Firstly, they must have binding jurisdiction over governments and companies for documented, repeated violations.
Secondly, satellite and concession data must be admitted as evidence and published openly. Thirdly, penalties must include fines, suspension of concessions and personal liability for directors.
Lastly, lenders must be held liable, as they finance the companies behind these fires. A 2019 Forests & Finance report counted about US$19 billion in loans and underwriting to 17 groups linked to Indonesia's fires between 2015 and August 2019.
Malaysian banks were the third-largest source, at about US$2.3 billion, behind China and Indonesia.
I would base the tribunal in Singapore. Its strong institutions and zero tolerance for lax standards, rent-seeking and nepotism make it a credible host. But hosting must come with safeguards.
Singapore suffers from the haze, yet its financial institutions also profit from financing groups linked to the fires. Judges should therefore come from countries not involved in the cases, with strict recusal rules to prevent conflicts of interest.
We are entering an era of climate conflict. We are at war with the planet, and the planet does not negotiate.
Young people across Asean have understood this. They have grown up under the same smoke as their parents, and they will not accept another round of statements of concern.
Asean needs a code of conduct with penalties for breaking it, applied equally to governments and boardrooms alike.
PIAL KHADILLA
Managing director — Asean
Global Institute For Tomorrow (GIFT)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shooting range tests leadership skills of senior civil servants
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Senior civil servants were put through a different kind of leadership test when a shooting sports activity was incorporated into the Advanced Leadership and Management Programme (ALMP) Series 89 No. 4/2026.
The activity was designed to assess participants' ability to plan, manage and coordinate programmes while reinforcing discipline, teamwork and compliance with safety procedures.
National Institute of Public Administration (INTAN) director Dr Mohd Zabri Yusoff said the shooting exercise was more than an introduction to the sport, serving as a practical platform for participants to sharpen their leadership and management skills.
He said the month-long programme emphasised systematic planning, effective coordination and proper implementation to ensure activities achieved their intended objectives.
"Among the aspects we emphasise is how participants plan a programme from the beginning, ensure safety briefings are conducted and carry out activities in accordance with established rules and regulations.
"When they return to their respective agencies, they must ensure that every programme and administrative matter is conducted in compliance with the relevant procedures and regulations," he said at the Shapadu Shooting Range in Precinct 20 today.
Zabri said safety, discipline and adherence to regulations were essential elements in developing effective leadership among senior government officers.
He said the hands-on approach allowed participants to appreciate the importance of meticulous planning, effective coordination and structured implementation in achieving organisational goals.
"The ALMP is a competency development programme that focuses on leadership assessment and strengthening management skills among senior public sector officers, including those holding JUSA C positions.
"The programme brings together officers from various service schemes and professional backgrounds, providing opportunities for them to exchange experiences and establish collaborative networks across government departments and agencies," he said.
He said the professional relationships developed throughout the programme should extend beyond the training period.
He said participants were encouraged to leverage these connections upon returning to their respective agencies to strengthen inter-agency cooperation and collaboration.
"We hope that when participants return to their respective agencies, the relationships established during the programme can be utilised, particularly among senior management, to strengthen cooperation and collaboration," he said.
He added that incorporating shooting sports into the programme reflected INTAN's emphasis on experiential learning in developing public sector leaders.
The approach, he said, reinforced the importance of planning, coordination, procedural compliance and teamwork in ensuring effective public administration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Podcaster to be called up over ex-journalist's Sentul drug claims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police will summon a podcaster to assist in an investigation into claims made on a podcast about drug dealing near the Sentul police headquarters.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said statements had so far been recorded from four people.
The case is being investigated under Section 505 of the Penal Code for statements conducing to public mischief and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act for misuse of network facilities.
The offences are punishable by jail terms and a fine.
"We will refer the case to the prosecution as soon as possible," he said on the sidelines of a Taman Angkat Amanita programme.
Fadil said people sharing their experiences on podcasts must do so responsibly to avoid misleading the public or disrupting public order.
"Give us time to complete our investigation," he said.
On Oct 20, Sentul police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said police would record a statement from a former journalist who appeared as a guest on the podcast.
This followed a police report over claims made on the podcast about an incident in 2016.
The former journalist claimed he had monitored drug dealing at a disused house of worship near a police station in Sentul.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Farhash files second defamation suit against Rafizi over podcast remarks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Businessman Datuk Seri Farhash Wafa Salvador Rizal Mubarak has initiated legal proceedings against former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli over allegedly defamatory statements made about him in a podcast.
Farhash's lawyer, Datuk Seri Rajan Navaratnam, said the writ and statement of claim were filed on Oct 23, with the court documents in the process of being served on Rafizi in accordance with the relevant procedures.
In a statement issued on behalf of his client, Rajan said the legal action stemmed from a podcast titled "Dari Umno ke PKR: Zetrix – Kerajaan Bertukar, Kroni Berpindah? | YBM #68", published on Rafizi's YouTube channel on Oct 16.
The podcast, which runs for about three hours and 14 minutes, contains statements concerning Farhash's alleged business interests, corporate relationships, purported links to political figures, and allegations relating to cronyism and government contract procurement.
Rajan said this was the second legal action initiated by Farhash against Rafizi.
"Our client maintains that the repeated publication of defamatory statements concerning him is tainted with malicious intent and has the effect of tarnishing his reputation.
"Therefore, our client considers it necessary to take legal action against Datuk Seri Mohd Rafizi Ramli," he said.
He said Farhash took the allegations seriously and believed such matters should be addressed through the proper legal process and determined based on the evidence and applicable law.
"As solicitors for our client, we do not intend to litigate this matter through the media or engage in public exchanges concerning the merits of the case.
"Ultimately, our client leaves the matter to the court to decide," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Some foreigners marry elderly Malaysian women to register vehicles, says RTD
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Foreigners are resorting to marrying elderly Malaysian women, including widows and single mothers, to register vehicles in their spouses' names in a bid to circumvent stricter enforcement against foreign drivers.
Road Transport Department (RTD) senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said investigations had revealed that some foreigners were targeting Malaysian women aged 60 and above, promising to marry them in exchange for allowing their names to be used for vehicle registration.
He said it was a new modus operandi adopted by foreign drivers in response to intensified enforcement operations since July.
"These foreigners are targeting women aged 60 and above, particularly single mothers, widows and unmarried women.
"They make sweet promises of marriage to persuade these women to allow their names to be used for vehicle registration.
"Some even go through with the marriage solely for the purpose of using their spouses' names," he told reporters at the Advanced Leadership and Management Programme (ALMP) Series 89 No. 4/2026 at the Shapadu Shooting Range in Precinct 20 today.
Kifli described the tactic as dangerous, warning Malaysians against allowing their personal details to be exploited for vehicle ownership.
He said the department had stepped up enforcement under Op Pewa following instructions from RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli in July.
Under the stricter enforcement measures, both foreign drivers and vehicle owners would face action if offences were detected.
"We will issue summonses to both the driver and the vehicle owner, while the vehicles involved will be seized.
"We will not offer compounds, meaning these cases will be brought to court.
"This is to demonstrate how seriously we view these offences, as action will be taken against both the driver and the owner," he said.
He said RTD had issued a total of 523,035 summons notices under Op Pewa between 2024 and Oct 15 this year.
Of the total, 183,300 notices were issued in 2024, followed by 191,676 last year and 148,059 so far this year.
He advised Malaysians against renting out their vehicles or allowing them to be used by foreigners who were not legally permitted to drive.
"We need the cooperation of all Malaysians to ensure that foreign drivers do not continue operating freely on our roads.
"If Malaysians refuse to allow their vehicles to be used by these foreigners, they will not be able to drive on our roads," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two foreigners held over dead baby found in Bangsar rubbish bin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have detained two foreigners in connection with the discovery of a dead baby girl in a rubbish bin in Abdullah Hukum, Bangsar, yesterday.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the suspects, a 23-year-old man and a 31-year-old woman, were arrested in Brickfields following investigations and tip-offs from the public.
"We believe they are linked to this case, and investigations are ongoing.
"We also appreciate the information provided by the public, which helped police track them down," he said at a press conference after the Wangsa Maju police headquarters Amanita Adoptive Park programme at PPR Laksamana, Jalan Peel, here today.
Asked whether the suspects were married, Fadil said it was still under investigation.
He said the baby was believed to have been around seven months into the pregnancy when Alam Flora workers found her body at a waste disposal area near Abdullah Hukum.
The case is being investigated under Section 318 of the Penal Code.
Brickfields district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said yesterday that police received a report of the discovery at 10.43am.
The body was found in a rubbish bin in an apartment complex before being sent to the Kuala Lumpur Hospital Forensic Unit for a post-mortem.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Malaysia ready to seek Gulf assistance to help Indonesia fight forest fires
Article:
REMBAU: Malaysia is prepared to provide any form of assistance to Indonesia in tackling transboundary haze, including seeking support from Gulf countries if necessary.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia understood the difficulties faced by Indonesia in managing extensive forest fires in areas far from its borders.
He said he would contact his Indonesian counterpart, Arrmanatha Christiawan Nasir, soon to discuss the assistance required.
"I also agreed with United Arab Emirates Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah Zayed Al Nahyan yesterday when he said that if assistance was needed, he was prepared to work with other countries to provide it.
"If Indonesia requires assistance, I will raise the matter with my counterparts in the Gulf countries to provide whatever help is needed," he told reporters after presenting Deepavali contributions to recipients in the Rantau state constituency at Dewan Orang Ramai Rantau here today.
Mohamad said Malaysia could not remain silent as forest fires in Indonesia also affected neighbouring countries, but any assistance operation would need to take safety considerations into account.
The Rembau member of Parliament said firefighting operations faced major challenges because the fires were located deep in remote areas, while thick haze had also reduced visibility.
He said developed countries such as Canada and the United States had also experienced forest fires, including those in Los Angeles that claimed many lives.
"It is easy for us to talk about it here, but imagine if the fires were 1,000km or even 500km from residential areas. There would be no other option but to use aircraft. However, aircraft would also be unable to carry out firefighting operations because of limited visibility," he said.
Meanwhile, Mohamad said Malaysia was prepared to provide humanitarian assistance to Yemen following discussions with Yemen's Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Minister, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, yesterday.
He also expressed hope that the civil war in Yemen could be brought to an end, saying the conflict had brought no benefits to the country's people and had left 22 million people bearing its consequences, including many facing starvation.
"Malaysia has expressed its sympathy and is prepared to participate in any relief mission or provide assistance.
"We also call on the parties with interests in the conflict from outside Yemen to come to the negotiating table so that the Yemeni people can enjoy a peaceful and prosperous life," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Pas almost certain to contest three Sarawak seats, says state chief
Article:
KUCHING: Pas will likely contest three state seats in the coming Sarawak election, says the Islamist party's state chief, Mohammad Arifiriazul Paijo.
He said the party was eyeing Semariang, Sebuyau and Beting Maro, although the final decision rested with the Pas central leadership.
He said Sarawak Pas had proposed contesting the three seats and that its election machinery in the areas was ready.
Arifiriazul said the party was also considering contesting another seat in northern Sarawak, either within the Bintulu or Sibuti parliamentary constituency.
However, he said Pas was not ready to disclose which seat it was considering.
Arifiriazul said they have also shortlisted candidates for the three seats.
On whether Pas would contest on its own or with other parties, he said discussions with several political partners were still ongoing and had yet to be finalised.
However, he said the outcome of those talks would not affect Pas' decision to contest the three seats, whether as part of a coalition or on its own.
Asked whether Pas could become part of the state government if it won any seats, he said the matter would only be decided when the time came.
"We are contesting this election to serve the local people and provide the best possible service to communities in the areas we contest.
Arifiriazul said Pas' victory in Sabah in the recent state election had also boosted morale among its 8,000 members in Sarawak.
Last night, Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the coalition, which Pas leads, had
yet to decide
on contesting in the Sarawak election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DBP honours Berita Harian, Harian Metro for strengthening use of Bahasa Melayu
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Berita Harian (BH) and Harian Metro (HM) have been recognised by Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) for their contributions to promoting and strengthening the use of Bahasa Melayu.
Both publications received the Hadiah Citra Bahasa Sahabat DBP 2026 at the launch of the 2026 National Language Month at Padang Kota here.
BH group editor Zulkifli Jalil and HM group editor Husain Jahit received the awards.
The Hadiah Citra Bahasa Sahabat DBP recognises organisations from the public and private sectors, as well as non-governmental organisations, for their contributions and commitment to promoting the national language.
Recipients receive a certificate of appreciation and RM5,000 in collaboration funding to organise literary bazaar activities.
The ceremony also saw the presentation of the Hadiah Citra Bahasa 2026, which recognises high achievement in Bahasa Melayu proficiency assessments. Recipients received RM3,000.
The Anugerah Ikon Bahasa 2026 was presented to lyricist and writer Datuk Habsah Hassan, professional emcee Terence Joseph Dass and Penang Mufti Associate Professor Datuk Dr Mohd Suki Othman for their contributions to upholding the national language.
Each recipient received RM2,000, a certificate of appreciation and books published by DBP.
The awards were presented by Education Ministry deputy director-general (Professional Development Sector) Datuk Amzan Abd Malek.
Husain said HM would continue to champion Bahasa Melayu at both national and international levels.
He said the recognition reflected the newspaper's continued commitment to promoting the national language through its media platforms and initiatives.
"We are proud to receive this award, as it shows that HM continues to be recognised," he said.
Husain said HM had recently organised a pantun competition in collaboration with DBP and DRB-HICOM to promote the Malay language and preserve its literary heritage.
He said pantun, a traditional Malay poetic form, remained an important part of Bahasa Melayu and a valuable medium for nurturing public appreciation of the language.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli said young people should use Bahasa Melayu wisely and preserve its integrity as a reflection of their identity.
He said the tendency to modify the language on social media to suit individual preferences should not come at the expense of its proper use.
"If we look at social media, much of our language has been modified to suit their tastes. However, we should preserve the national language because it reflects our identity," he said.
Zulkifli also highlighted the role of newspapers in helping young people improve their language proficiency, particularly in grammar and writing.
He encouraged students to read newspapers, including BH, the New Straits Times (NST) and other publications circulated in schools.
"Newspapers use language that is proper and somewhat academic. I hope students will return to reading newspapers, especially to learn from the grammar used," he said.
He said regular exposure to well-written news articles could help students better understand Bahasa Melayu and use it appropriately in everyday communication.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man reported missing for 5 days found dead in Kajang
Article:
KAJANG: A man who was reported missing by his family five days ago was found dead in a car at a supermarket car park in Jalan Impian Mahkota last night.
District police chief assistant commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said police received a report about the discovery of the car at 11.29pm.
"Initial investigations found a man, believed to be in his 50s, lying unconscious in the driver's seat of a Perodua Axia.
"The engine was off and the car was locked from the inside," he said.
He said police sought the assistance of Fire and Rescue Department personnel to open the car door before medical personnel from Kajang Hospital examined the victim and pronounced him dead.
He said police received a missing person report last Tuesday after the man's family members were unable to contact him.
"Preliminary investigations have so far found no foul play at the scene or on the deceased. The case has been classified as a sudden death report (SDR).
"Further investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the incident and his death," he said in a statement today.
Those with information about the incident is urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Shisheewady Ruzani at 016-856 5670 or the nearest police station.
Earlier, several photographs went viral showing police and Fire and Rescue Department personnel examining a parked car near a supermarket.
Following this, several social media users claimed that the man inside the car was their family member who had been reported missing five days earlier and was found at the location.
The man and the car were found about 15 minutes from where he allegedly lived.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New-generation MyKad records 275,785 issuances in first month
Article:
KULAI: The National Registration Department (JPN) has issued 275,785 new-generation MyKad nationwide since its launch on Sept 17 until Oct 20, with Johor recording the highest number at 31,392 cards.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures reflected a positive response from the public to the new-generation MyKad, which comes with enhanced security features.
He said the new-generation MyKad incorporates 53 security features, compared with 23 in the previous version. These include a transparent window, QR code, ultraviolet features, hologram and microtext.
The enhancements were introduced to ensure the identity card's security features remained relevant to technological advancements, following about 12 years of use of the previous MyKad generation.
"JPN has taken steps to further upgrade the security features. That is why we call it the new-generation MyKad," he said.
"Johor recorded the highest number, with 31,392 cards issued, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 29,601, Selangor (26,736), Sarawak (25,642) and Sabah (22,523)," he told a press conference after officiating the 78th National Registration Day celebration and the launch of the MADANI Adopted Village and MADANI Adopted School initiatives at the Kampung Melayu Sedenak Multipurpose Hall here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the public need not rush to replace their MyKad, as JPN had assured them that the supply of cards was sufficient to meet demand.
He said about 24 million existing MyKad were currently in circulation, while JPN received an average of 200,000 applications a month for various purposes, including new identity cards, replacements for damaged cards and MyKad issuance to those turning 18.
He said possession of a MyKad was becoming increasingly important due to various government initiatives requiring its use, including purchases of petrol and cooking oil, as well as the redemption of Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA).
"We do not have any projections. We will continue as usual and serve the public. What matters is ensuring that the card supply is sufficient to meet demand from those who choose to switch to the new-generation MyKad," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Zahid: BN sticks to 7-seat pact with PN despite bid for more
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) will honour its agreement to allocate seven seats it is not contesting to Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the Melaka state election, despite calls for additional seats.
BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the allocation had been agreed upon and would stand.
"I have heard about efforts to seek additional seats, but we already have a pact, an agreement to allow them to contest the seven seats BN is not contesting, which we have left to PN's component parties to distribute among themselves.
"That is the decision for now, and we will stand by what we have mutually agreed upon," he told reporters after the Ulul Albab Huffaz Graduation and Excellence Appreciation Ceremony here today.
Yesterday, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said PN hoped to negotiate for one or two additional seats beyond the seven announced earlier.
Zahid had previously confirmed that negotiations on a political understanding with Pas had been concluded, with BN to contest 21 seats and the remaining seven allocated to Pas and its political allies.
The Election Commission has set Oct 31 for nomination, Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 for polling.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar wants thorough probe into death in police custody
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed police to conduct a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly while in police custody.
Anwar said he had taken note of the presence of Noorizwan's family, who had come to submit an appeal to him today, and expressed his condolences over the death.
He said he understood the grief and anxiety faced by the family, who were awaiting answers about the circumstances surrounding Noorizwan's death.
"I have taken note of the presence of the family of the late Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, who came to submit an appeal letter to me today. I am deeply saddened by his death and understand the grief and anxiety of the family, who are awaiting answers," he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar said he was scheduled to attend several engagements in Melaka today and had therefore delegated an officer to receive the letter and listen directly to the issues raised by the family.
He said he had also contacted Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail to obtain further information about the case.
"I have also contacted the Inspector-General of Police to obtain further information about this case and stressed that the investigation must be conducted thoroughly, transparently and without compromise, with developments in the investigation communicated to the family," he said.
Noorizwan's family earlier
submitted a memorandum to Anwar
at his house in Bandar Sungai Long this morning, appealing for his intervention in the case.
The family, accompanied by Lawyers for Liberty, called for immediate action and justice following his death while in detention at the Cheras district police headquarters, where he had been held since Sept 19.
Noorizwan died at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz on Oct 1 after being taken there for treatment the previous day.
His
preliminary post-mortem report
stated that he had sustained multiple bodily injuries.
The family is seeking answers about the circumstances surrounding his death and has called for a thorough investigation into the matter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family of dead detainee seeks PM's help
Article:
KAJANG: The family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, who died while in police custody at Cheras district police headquarters, has sought the help of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar for a transparent investigation into his death.
The family turned up at Anwar's residence in Bandar Sungai Long this morning to hand over a memorandum to the prime minister's representative.
The family accompanied by their lawyers gathered at the guardhouse before being allowed into the compound.
The memorandum, submitted by Noorizwan's younger brother Nooranis Zulkeﬂy and lawyers from Lawyers for Liberty (LFL), said the family had serious concerns over the injuries found on the deceased's body during the post-mortem.
The family is now seeking immediate action and a transparent investigation into his death.
A post-mortem at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) revealed no damage to his internal organs but confirmed multiple external bodily injuries, police said.
The cause of death remains undetermined and has been classified as "pending laboratory analysis" while pathologists await toxicology and histology findings from the Chemistry Department.
Noorizwan was detained by police on Sept 19 by Cheras police for suspected drug possession and theft/housebreaking offences.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus had said that Noorizwan had been managed in strict compliance with standard operating procedures before suddenly falling ill.
After 11 days in detention, he was transferred to HCTM on Sept 30 for emergency treatment and was pronounced dead early on Oct 1.
Fadil also highlighted that the deceased carried 44 prior criminal records, consisting of 18 narcotics infractions and 26 other offences, and had allegedly admitted to 17 unsolved break-ins across Cheras.
Bukit Aman's Criminal Investigation and Deaths in Custody Unit (USJKT) is leading the inquiry and to date have interviewed 78 individuals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain, strong winds in nine states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 6 pm today.
The warning covers Perlis, Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak), as well as Langkawi and Kubang Pasu in Kedah.
The warning also applies to Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru in Johor; Cameron Highlands in Pahang; Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus and Setiu in Terengganu; and Jeli, Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas and Tumpat in Kelantan.
In Sabah, the affected areas are Kudat; Sandakan; Tawau (Tawau, Kunak and Semporna); the West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang and Tuaran); and the Interior (Tambunan, Sook, Keningau, Beaufort, Tenom, Sipitang and Pensiangan).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Bintulu (Tatau and Sebauh); Kapit (Kapit and Belaga); Limbang; Miri (Marudi, Bario, Beluru and Telang Usan); and Sibu (Selangau). — Bernama

Title: Two Malaysians injured in Typhoon Champi recovering in Taiwan hospitals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Two Malaysian nationals who sustained minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi in Taiwan are receiving treatment at separate hospitals and their conditions are reported to be stable.
Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC) President Bong Yik Jui said the two, both 57, were receiving treatment at Dali Jen Ai Hospital in Taichung and Miaoli Daqian Hospital in Miaoli, respectively.
“We contacted both individuals separately and confirmed that they are in stable condition,” he told Bernama.
He added that one of the Malaysians had been discharged from hospital after receiving treatment.
Bong said the MFTC would closely monitor developments related to Typhoon Champi, particularly its implications for the safety and welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan.
“MFTC will remain in contact with the Malaysian community through existing communication channels,” he said.
Media reported that Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, leaving one dead and more than 500 injured. The typhoon also damaged hundreds of buildings, disrupted electricity supply, and forced flight cancellations.
As of August, this year, there were 34,833 Malaysians in Taiwan, including 7,615 students.
Bong urged Malaysians residing in or visiting Taiwan to monitor local weather advisories and adhere to safety instrutions and evacuation orders issued by local authorities.
Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information concerning other Malaysian nationals who may require assistance in the affected areas, are urged to contact MFTC in Taipei at +886 972 349 343 or via email at
mwtaipei@kln.gov.my
.
Bong also urged Malaysians in Taiwan to register and regularly update their contact details through the e-Konsular portal at
https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my
to facilitate timely communication and consular assistance, particularly during emergencies.
He also encouraged Malaysians to follow the MFTC’s social media channels for the latest updates and advisories.
The MFTC serves as Malaysia’s official representative office in Taipei, performing consular functions similar to those of Malaysian diplomatic and consular missions abroad and providing assistance and support to Malaysians in Taiwan. — Bernama

Title: Haze spreads to five Sarawak spots while Klang Valley air improves slightly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Air quality deteriorated further this afternoon, with 23 monitoring stations recording unhealthy readings on the Air Pollutant Index (API) at 4.00pm, up from 21 in the morning, according to the Department of Environment (DOE).
Of the 68 stations nationwide, 23 registered readings in the unhealthy range of 101 to 200, while 39 recorded moderate air quality and six remained in the good tier. No station entered very unhealthy or hazardous territory.
Seremban in Negeri Sembilan logged the worst air quality in the country at 172, up from 169 at 10.00am. Elsewhere in the state, Nilai recorded 166, while Port Dickson improved to 140. Melaka saw all three of its monitoring stations remain in the unhealthy tier, led by Bukit Rambai at 163, Bandaraya Melaka at 160, and Alor Gajah at 158.
Johor remained the worst-affected state, with eight stations in the unhealthy bracket after Kota Tinggi joined the list at 151. Batu Pahat and Kluang climbed to 166 and 165 respectively, with Kluang matching Larkin, which eased to 165 from 169. Tangkak registered 162, Pasir Gudang 161, Segamat 155, and Pengerang 154.
In East Malaysia, Sarawak saw the sharpest rise in affected areas, expanding from three to five unhealthy stations. IPD Serian rose to 160, Sri Aman to 157, and Kapit to 153, while Kuching and Samarahan entered the bracket at 155 and 153. In Pahang, Rompin became the state's sole unhealthy locality after logging 141.
Conversely, parts of the Klang Valley showed slight improvement. Batu Muda and Cheras in Kuala Lumpur eased to 159 and 141, while Putrajaya improved to 118 from 151 in the morning. Petaling Jaya and Klang, which recorded 124 and 113 earlier in the day, dropped back into the moderate range.
Under the API system, readings between 101 and 200 are categorised as unhealthy. Health authorities advise high-risk individuals, including children, the elderly, and those with heart or respiratory conditions, to limit prolonged outdoor physical activity and wear face masks outside.

Title: Drunk driver crashes into DBKL road crew, killing supervisor on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A road maintenance supervisor was killed and a lorry driver injured early today when a suspected drunk driver crashed into them along Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the 26-year-old driver recorded a breath alcohol level of 64mg/100ml, NST reported.
The suspect was arrested and remanded for three days until Monday to assist in investigations.
The crash occurred at around 5.00am when the car, travelling from Jalan Damansara towards Jalan Parlimen, lost control and struck two workers in the left lane.
"The victim, a supervisor, was pronounced dead while receiving treatment, while another worker, a 49-year-old lorry driver, sustained injuries to his head and right hand. The lorry driver is receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital. The car driver escaped uninjured.
"The five workers, comprising a supervisor, a lorry driver and three Bangladeshi workers, had been carrying out warning sign installation works under a Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) contract.
"The work began at 11pm on Oct 23 and ended at 4am today," he said in a statement.
Zamzuri said the case is being investigated under Sections 44(1)(b) and 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs causing death and injury.
Police have urged anyone who witnessed the crash to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or visit the nearest police station.

Title: End of the road: Sabah police nab Beverly Hills murder suspect wanted for over 17 years
Article:
PENAMPANG, Oct 24 — A 42-year-old murder suspect on the run for more than 17 years has finally been arrested in Sabah over a 2009 homicide in Penampang.
Penampang acting police chief Assistant Superintendent Arisanti Aziz said investigators detained the man at a house in Kolombong, Inanam on Thursday.
“The arrest followed our continuous efforts to track down the suspect and investigate the case,” she said in a statement today.
Police had sought the suspect over the death of a man in Beverly Hills, Penampang on April 11, 2009.
“The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years.
“If the death penalty is not imposed, the offender is also liabe to at least 12 strokes of the cane, subject to applicable legal provisions,” she said.
Arisanti added that the arrest demonstrates the police force’s commitment to combating crime, including solving cold cases and bringing long-sought suspects to court.

Title: Missing man found dead in locked car at Kajang supermarket car park
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A man who went missing five days ago was found dead inside a locked car parked outside a supermarket in Jalan Impian Mahkota late last night, ending a desperate search by his family that had circulated on social media.
Kajang district police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said authorities were alerted to the stationary vehicle at 11.29pm after passers-by spotted a motionless figure in the front cabin,
NST
reported.
"Initial investigations found a man, believed to be in his 50s, lying unconscious in the driver's seat of a Perodua Axia.
"The engine was off and the car was locked from the inside," he said.
Responding officers enlisted the help of the Fire and Rescue Department to pry open the locked doors, after which medical personnel from Hospital Kajang examined the victim and pronounced him dead at the scene.
Naazron confirmed that the victim's family had lodged a missing person report last Tuesday after repeated attempts to reach his mobile phone went unanswered. The vehicle was discovered approximately 15 minutes away from his residence.
"Preliminary investigations have so far found no foul play at the scene or on the deceased. The case has been classified as a sudden death report (SDR).
"Further investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the incident and his death," he said.
Yesterday, images circulated online showing police cruisers and fire rescue trucks cordoning off a vehicle in the supermarket car park.

Title: King and Queen offer prayers for late Terengganu prince Tengku Baderul Zaman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The King, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, and the Queen, Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, have extended their condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, and the entire Terengganu royal family on the passing of Sultan Mizan’s younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
In a post on His Majesty’s official Facebook page, the King and Queen also prayed that the late Tengku Baderul Zaman’s soul be showered with barakah (divine blessings) and mercy, that all his sins be forgiven, and that he be placed among the faithful.
“Condolences to Al-Wathiqu Billah Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah and the entire Terengganu Royal Family on the passing of Dato’ Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
“Prayers are raised that the soul of the late Tengku Baderul Zaman be showered with barakah and mercy, that all his sins be forgiven, and that he be placed among the faithful,” the post read.
Tengku Baderul Zaman was reported to have passed away at 1.20 am today at a hospital in Kuala Lumpur. — Bernama

Title: PM extends condolences to Terengganu Sultan over brother’s death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, on the passing of His Royal Highness’s younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Allah SWT would shower His mercy upon Tengku Baderul Zaman’s soul, grant him forgiveness and place him among the righteous.
“May the Sultan of Terengganu and the entire royal family be granted fortitude and strength in facing this deeply felt loss. Al-Fatihah,” the post read.
Tengku Baderul Zaman died at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital here. — Bernama

Title: BN rejects Perikatan request for additional seats in Melaka election
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 24 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will stick to its agreement to allocate seven seats it is not contesting to Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the Melaka state election, despite attempts to secure additional seats.
BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the allocation had been agreed upon under a mutual agreement, which BN would honour.
“I have heard about efforts to seek additional seats, but we already have a pact, an agreement to allow them to contest the seven seats BN is not contesting, which we have left to PN’s component parties to distribute among themselves.
“That is the decision for now, and we will stand by what we have mutually agreed upon,” he told reporters after the Ulul Albab Huffaz Graduation and Excellence Appreciation Ceremony here today.
Yesterday, PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man was reported as saying that PN hoped to hold negotiations to secure an additional one or two seats in addition to the seven announced earlier.
Ahmad Zahid had previously confirmed that negotiations on a political understanding with PAS had been finalised, with BN to contest 21 seats while the remaining seven would be allocated to PAS and its political allies.
The Election Commission (EC) has set October 31 for nomination, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling in the state election. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia stands ready to assist Yemen, backs renewed negotiations
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 24 — Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian assistance to Yemen, while urging all parties in the protracted conflict in the country to return to the negotiation table and look for a diplomatic solution.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia empathises with the suffering of the Yemeni people who have to endure the effects of the protracted civil war, including famine and hardship in getting basic necessities.
He said the matter was brought up by his counterpart, Yemen’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, who shared on the latest developments in the country via a phone call on Thursday.
“Malaysia stands ready to participate in any relief mission or deliver assistance to countries that require it, to the best of our ability,” he told reporters after handing over Deepavali festive contributions at the Rantau community hall here, today.
Mohamad said the conflict must be brought to an end as it brings no benefit to the estimated 22 million affected inhabitants and instead inflicts prolonged suffering.
In light of this, he urged foreign stakeholders to play a constructive role by returning to negotiation table to bring peace and prosperity to the people of Yemen.
He said diplomatic efforts need to be prioritised in order to prevent the conflict from dragging on and undermining regional stability. — Bernama

Title: Government to establish Veterans’ Day for MAF veterans
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The government plans to establish Veterans’ Day to honour the service and sacrifice of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a specific date for the celebration will be proposed to the Cabinet soon for the government’s approval.
“It will serve as a recognition, a formal acknowledgement that we honour veterans.
“It will also certainly foster closer ties and greater public appreciation for MAF veterans in our country,” he said at the opening ceremony of the 100th National General Assembly of the Malaysian Armed Forces Veterans Association (PVATM) here today.
Also present were Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman and PVATM president Datuk Sharuddin Omar.
In other developments, Mohamed Khaled said companies awarded major government contracts must provide job opportunities for MAF veterans to ensure they continue to have a place in the economy after completing their service.
He said the Ministry of Defence (Mindef) will monitor the implementation of the initiative to ensure veterans also benefit from these job opportunities.
On Tabung Pahlawan (Warriors’ Fund), he said collections have risen every year, reflecting public appreciation for the contribution of armed forces veterans to safeguarding the nation’s peace and security.
He said collections increased from RM1.3 million in 2023-2024 to RM2.19 million in 2024-2025 and RM3.35 million in 2025-2026.
He added that collections for 2026-2027 have so far reached RM4.35 million, against a target of RM5 million. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar calls for thorough investigation into detainee’s death in police custody
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly in police custody.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he had contacted Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail to obtain further information on the case and ensure that updates on the investigation were conveyed to the deceased’s family.
He said he understood the family’s grief and anxiety as they awaited answers regarding Noorizwan’s death.
“I acknowledge the presence of the late Noorizwan’s family to submit an appeal letter to me today. I am deeply saddened by his passing and understand the family’s grief and anxiety as they await answers,” he said.
Anwar, who was scheduled to attend several programmes in Melaka today, said he had delegated his officers to receive the appeal letter and listen to the concerns raised by the family.
Media reports previously said police were still awaiting the full report from the Chemistry Department and the pathology findings to determine the actual cause of the man’s death on Oct 1.
